selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: After leaving the gathering of the prophets, where was the traveler invited next?
questions.answer: He was invited to the learning circle of pure and truthful scholars who support the prophets’ message with strong proofs.

questions.question: What was special about the scholars’ way of defending belief?
questions.answer: They used the strongest and clearest proofs.

questions.question: What was the main purpose of their work in that classroom?
questions.answer: Their purpose was to establish the truths of faith with decisive evidence.

questions.question: Why is their agreement important even though they differed from one another?
questions.answer: Because they had different abilities and viewpoints, yet still agreed on the main beliefs, which shows the truth is very strong.

questions.question: Why does their agreement despite those differences strengthen their case?
questions.answer: Because agreement among diverse thinkers shows the conclusion is based on truth, not copying or pressure.

questions.question: What challenge does the passage set for anyone who wants to doubt all of them?
questions.answer: The doubter would need to make it believable that a huge number of sharp and intelligent people all reached one conclusion incorrectly.

questions.question: What idea is taught by the example of a person shutting his eyes?
questions.answer: Refusing to see the truth does not change reality; it only darkens things for that person himself.

questions.question: What does the image of closing one’s eyes teach about disbelief?
questions.answer: It teaches that disbelief cannot erase the truth; it only blinds the person who rejects it.

questions.question: What kind of power did the traveler notice in their classroom that was not physical?
questions.answer: He noticed moral and spiritual power.

questions.question: Why did the traveler feel drawn to the scholars after meeting the prophets?
questions.answer: Because he had tasted the truth through faith and was ready to learn from scholars who explained the prophets’ message with clear evidence.

questions.question: In relation to the prophets, what role did these scholars have?
questions.answer: They confirmed the prophets’ claims by giving powerful evidence.

questions.question: What did the traveler observe when he entered their classroom?
questions.answer: He observed a vast number of brilliant scholars proving the matters of belief.

questions.question: What makes their agreement especially meaningful?
questions.answer: Their agreement matters even more because they were not all alike in skill or perspective, yet they still reached the same main conclusions.

questions.question: What kinds of differences existed among the scholars?
questions.answer: They differed in ability and in how they looked at things.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about doubting all of them at once?
questions.answer: It suggests that such doubt is unreasonable unless one could prove that many intelligent people can unite on one result without truth behind it.

questions.question: What lesson about truth is taught by the image of day and night?
questions.answer: Truth stays clear like daylight even if someone personally refuses to admit it.

questions.question: How far did the scholars’ light reach?
questions.answer: It reached half of the world.

questions.question: Why could the people of denial not destroy what was in that classroom?
questions.answer: Because the classroom held a spiritual and moral strength stronger than all their combined efforts.

questions.question: What happened to the traveler after he benefited from the prophets’ gathering?
questions.answer: He was led to a class of truthful scholars who confirm the prophets’ teachings.

questions.question: How are the scholars described besides being knowledgeable?
questions.answer: They are also described as sincere, refined, and very trustworthy.

questions.question: How strong were their proofs described to be?
questions.answer: Their proofs were so solid and deep that they left no room for doubt.

questions.question: Did the passage say the scholars were identical in how they thought?
questions.answer: No, it says they differed in capacity and viewpoint.

questions.question: How does diversity among the scholars make their agreement more convincing?
questions.answer: Since they came from different levels and perspectives, their agreement looks earned through truth rather than sameness.

questions.question: Who welcomed the traveler after the assembly of the prophets?
questions.answer: A body of purified and truthful scholars welcomed him into their place of learning.
